review_scope: P10 reopened pre-GUI usability repair and cumulative P01-P10 integration on the declared QEMU profile
resolved_findings: Shell no longer drains foreground child stdin while checking cancellation. Console buffering preserves normal input, detects cancellation at saturation, and clears retained bytes on final session detach.
Binary cat redirection preserves raw bytes; invalid-text display converts bounded chunks rather than expanding an entire file beyond the shell heap.
Canonical terminal editing survives small ReadFile requests; actual Tiny Basic Backspace correction produces 123.
Ordinary storage checkpoints reserve journal capacity; bounded Win32 writes and large BASIC saves no longer exhaust one unbounded transaction.
Safe allocator NoSpace remains recoverable; backend-confirmed uncertain journal or device failures retain fail-closed behavior.
Multiple ordinary boots in one suite have separate staging directories, firmware variables, serial streams and QMP identities.
evidence_interpretation: The exact cumulative report is successful, certified P10, inputs_unchanged=true and failure=null. All required commands and all 116 checks pass. Current hashes of the exact 321 filtered source/build/contract inputs match its sorted source snapshot.

Independently rehashed all retained command stdout/stderr bindings, all 42 diagnostic scenario report/guest/serial bindings, both ordinary serials, the final ordinary raw disk, and all six outputs of three application rebuild pairs: 373 matching bindings. Expected scenario outcomes and all declared diagnostic markers were checked against retained raw serials.

The original cumulative guest gate retains 42 scenarios and both completed interactive diagnostic checks. Host test output totals 363 passing tests; the report also records strict target checks, Windows references and deterministic rebuilds.

Ordinary boot argv contains no test-token fw_cfg selection or isa-debug-exit device. Fresh private boots use the same persistent disk with distinct UUIDs. Native file operations, more than 32 namespace objects, copied executable admission, argv/environment/cwd propagation, denied system writes, malformed-image rejection and repeated process retirement have real terminal evidence.

Tiny Basic is pinned unchanged upstream C with an original narrow C/Win32 platform port. Both rebuilt PE copies have SHA256 1e00735caeb2387d4f5b9debec6990f84f3c656b499c38115a33a2dba13c9de3. That same binary runs on Windows and Door, producing 55 and 1024; actual Door interaction also covers corrected input, loops, save/load, fresh-boot argv loading and cancellation.

The independent raw-disk audit records a 229893-byte, 3300-line BASIC save, preserved native binary copies and durable user text. A subsequent unrelated user write succeeds. Saved and reopened raw disk hashes match. First ordinary shutdown retires 27 processes/threads with leaked=0; fresh boot and actual reboot retire 7 then 5 with leaked=0. Each cleanup reclaims eight DMA pages; fresh reopen and reboot perform zero writes and flushes.

Source inspection covered kernel generic-execute capture/retirement, broker capability ownership and session shutdown, ordinary terminal input, storage mutation/capacity handling, namespace schema3, original C runtime and ordinary-session evidence validation. Review findings were corrected and the final frozen cumulative run includes those corrections.
scope_limits: Finite source review and bounded host/guest qualification do not establish absence of every bug, all scheduler interleavings, or physical-hardware correctness.

This acceptance establishes the implemented useful text-mode pre-GUI profile on QEMU q35/TCG, one production vCPU and 2 GiB RAM, alongside inherited diagnostic/SMP regressions. It does not qualify GUI development or a complete desktop.

Tiny Basic is a third-party source port, not an independently distributed stock Windows executable. Its unchanged interpreter plus original platform glue does not establish broad EXE/DLL, UCRT, arbitrary external DLL loading, installer or general Windows application compatibility.

Production storage remains a constrained dense ext2/journal implementation: 32 MiB filesystem, fixed inode/catalog capacities and approximately 4 MiB per-file maximum. Paths, IPC messages, process resources and command arguments remain explicitly bounded.

The Tiny Basic port has ASCII filenames, four nonterminal file streams, a 384 KiB application heap, bounded formatting and unchanged upstream parsing limits. It is not hardened for hostile BASIC programs; application faults must remain isolated.
Development capability-based identity, credential/entropy limitations, absent network support and incomplete native standard-library coverage remain explicit boundaries.

Hashes establish identity within this trusted local workspace rather than external attestation. Phase ledger updates, documentation closure and launching the owner session are the coordinating agent responsibility.
cleanup: This review wrote only reports/critics/p10-readiness-critic.json. No source, contract, documentation, phase ledger or historical critic was modified; no broad test suite was rerun and no retained evidence was deleted.
